title: Turn 4 played — B 6-4: 1/11 (one man, via the 5)
instructions: Cut VID20260820105037 at t=94.5s and take the whole frame.
The board as the ledger leaves it after turn 4.

Turn 4's own pair, lying where it fell in the far half. DERIVED rather than read, which is what the sidecar's `diceDerived` says in a form a machine can check: a die this deep into the far half shows this camera a front face and a sliver of top, and neither up face is legible — a zoom was read as 6-5 on 2026-08-21 and that is what the correction replaces. A ten-pip one-man play out of the 1-point, with the 6-point blocked four deep, can only have been thrown 6-4. The front faces are consistent with it and do not settle it: a clean 5 on the left die, so its top is neither 2 nor 5; a diagonal run of three pips (possibly four) on the right, which excludes 3 and 4 from its top either way.
